div.head: Enclosure 4

p.hi: SUGGESTED PROCEDURES FOR POSTS IN DEALING WITH TERRORIST ACTS AGAINST AMERICANS ABROAD

list.label: A.
list.item: Study Washington procedure, policy considerations and press guidance (Enclosures 1, 2, and 3).
list.label: B.
list.item:
Devise a contingency plan for the post to dovetail into the Washington plan. Such a plan should consider: (1)
The composition of the local task force which would respond to likely contingencies. (2)
All agencies at the post must be fully cognizant of the plan and be contributing to it within their respective competences. (3)
Designated area or areas in which the task force would convene. (4)
Communications links (secure and otherwise) with Washington: cable, telephone, telecon, teleprinter, SSB. (5)
Local communications links which might be useful in a rescue operation, including walkie-talkies, commercial facilities, host government facilities. (6)
Rank order of decision-makers in the event the post’s ranking officers are held hostage by terrorists. (7)
[2 lines not declassified] (8)
[2 lines not declassified] (9)
Unique health factors of each employee such as heart condition, special medications. (10)
Coordination with subordinate posts so that plans dovetail. (11)
Press relations (see section on Press Guidance, Enclosure #3).
(12)
Likely host government contacts in a terrorist incident. (13)
Medical support for the hostages and for their families. (14)
Psychiatric or other behavioral science support which might be called in. (15)
Possible Washington support anticipated in personnel and material (if nearby posts cannot provide). (16)
Possible earmarking of emergency equipment. (Suggested check list attached.)

div.p:
The local task force commander might develop a check list along the following lines: (1)
FLASH or telephone to the Department, attention Operations Center, which will alert S/CCT, the geographic bureau concerned, another agency if the employee is non-State, and others as specified in the Washington task force procedures (Enclosure #1). (2)
Give fullest details, in consonance with good security if an open line is used, so that Washington can be of maximum support. Continue this process, bearing in mind the importance of a running telegraphic account of the incident for easy distribution in Washington for offices and agencies standing by to support the post in the rescue. Periodic, numbered SITREPS are the usual form. (3)
Establish contact with the Washington task force and agree on optional lines of communication and joint procedures. (4)
Convene and initiate actions of the task force as prearranged or as circumstances of the incident dictate.
(5)
Establish earliest contact with the host government, reminding them of their responsibilities in the rescue, agreeing on the primary objective of safe return of the hostages, offering all appropriate assistance, acquainting them as appropriate with US policy considerations, establishing permanent liaison in whatever and in as many channels as may be profitable, and agreeing on a joint press policy. (6)
Establish earliest contact with the family of the victim at the post and delegate an employee or employees to see that the family’s wishes and preoccupations are well considered. Advise the Washington task force which members of the family and Congress should be contacted in the emergency. (7)
Even though instructions from Washington may not have arrived, analyze the situation in the light of US and host government policy considerations and make recommendations regarding USG actions. Continue this process with periodic assessments and recommendations. (8)
Consider what additional precautionary measures might be taken by other Americans at the post, in the host country, or elsewhere. (9)
[text not declassified] (10)
Call the officer-in-charge of press relations to the task force and give him initial guidance.
Note items which the Chairman of the Washington task force will wish to discuss with the principal officer (Enclosure #1, Section IV).

note.p: If other agencies are reporting on the incident from a post, their messages should be slugged for the Department to the maximum extent possible.
